text:
Thom: FYI — Epsilon Corp hit a big 429 wave in prod EU about 10m ago. Customer says it started after a traffic spike from a nightly job. They sent a sample curl and logs.
Maria: ack. can you paste the exact curl + response headers? Also need request_id(s), model, endpoint, and whether they share a single API key across many users.
Thom: paste from customer: 
```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx\" -d '{"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
x-rate-limit-rpm: 120\nx-rate-limit-rpm-remaining: 0\nx-rate-limit-tpm: 600\nx-rate-limit-tpm-remaining: 120\ncontent-type: application/json\n
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "message": "RPM limit reached for org" }
```
Thom: they also included a short snippet of their client loop — they retry immediately (no jitter) and spin up 20 parallel workers at midnight to batch requests.
Maria: ok that explains it. looks like they hit the per-minute (RPM) ceiling then retries made it worse. classic retry storm.
Alex: quick triage checklist: 1) confirm org-level RPM from quota service 2) check gateway logs for pattern (same API key across many clients?) 3) verify we've applied per-second smoothing or burst window 4) find first 429 timestamp to get sample request_ids
Sam: queries you can run: 
```
# fetch gateway logs with request id window
kubectl logs deployment/gateway -n prod --since=30m | rg req_0a1b2c3d -n
# rate limit service counters (pseudo)
redis-cli HGETALL rl:org:epsilon-corp
```
Maria: immediate mitigation to tell customer: - reduce concurrency to <=5 workers - add exponential backoff with full jitter, base 500ms, cap 10s - stop immediate retries for 429s for at least 30s - re-run with sample requests and send us request_ids if they still happen :thumbsup:
Thom: customer is asking for a short-term quota bump while they rework the job. can we approve a temporary increase? @Ingrid any fast path?
Ingrid: I can do a one-off uplift for up to 24h if legal/entitlements are ok. Need org id, current plan, and estimated sustained RPM they expect. Also flag to sales if they want Dedicated.
Maria: Filing info needed from customer: org_id, example request_id, peak RPM estimate, whether they share key, timestamp window (start/end). I'll DM them a small checklist.
RateLimitBot: Automated notice: \"Rate limiter applied: org=epsilon-corp rule=rpm-120 window=60s action=reject\"
Alex: root cause summary (short): customer scheduled parallelized batch job that produces short spikes. They share a single API key for all workers so org-level RPM is concentrated, hitting rpm ceiling. Retries without jitter amplified the spike.
Sam: longer term fixes to suggest in guidance docs: - encourage token-per-worker pattern (per-user keys) - implement client-side token-bucket limiting - server-side smoothing: allow burst token budget for known scheduled jobs (requires support request) - encourage Dedicated/reserved capacity for predictable throughput
Thom: I added a sample reproduction script (sanitized) customer can run: 
```
# repro: spawn 20 workers that call the API in tight loop
python repro_burst.py --workers 20 --rate 10
```
Maria: please attach this to the ticket along with our retry guidance. I'll also add a short FAQ snippet for SDKs: 
```
# recommended retry policy (psuedocode)
backoff = jittered_exponential(base=0.5, cap=10)
for attempt in 1..N:
  resp = call_api()
  if resp.status == 429:
    sleep(backoff())
  else:
    break
```
Thom: we've opened a support ticket for temporary uplift. Ingrid — sent org details in DM.
Ingrid: got it. I'll raise a 24h +50% RPM uplift pending customer confirmation. cc @Maria for notes.
Alex: ops step: check if gateway smoothing policy is enabled for EU prod; if not, we should consider enabling per-org burst smoothing to avoid tight spikes taking down downstream pools. Will follow up.
DeployBot: Deploy notice: rate-limiter patch v2.4.1 rolled to canary at 1999999000, no errors reported.
Maria: owner action list: 1) Thom — collect request_ids + sample logs (due 30m) 2) Ingrid — handle uplift (due 15m) 3) Alex — check gateway smoothing + provide logs snippet (due 1h) 4) Sam — write replay instructions for engineering (due 2h) 5) Maria — update ticket with recommended retry policy and repro script (due 45m)
Thom: customer accepted the quick guidance and reduced concurrency. they saw 429s drop within ~2 minutes after backoff/jitter.
Maria: marking triage done for now. will re-open if they re-hit limits after uplift expires. closing notes saved to ticket. :white_check_mark:
